title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding notes on 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes'): X is a compact connected Riemann surface of genus g. K ⊂ X is a closed 'tame' subcomplex, for example a graph or a system of curves. The previous page builds the 'purified' pair (K̃, L̃) via K̃ = lim K_x. The components f ∈ F = π0(X−K) are open surfaces of genus g(f) with ν(f) ends ('bouts').

The top lines are a normalisation of the decomposition. The ends should be homotopically non-trivial, i.e. no complementary piece should be a trivial disc unless explicitly allowed. In 'le premier cas' the discs must be non-trivial. One also assumes π0(K) → π0(X) is surjective.

The aim is a parameter (moduli) count. Grothendieck compares the moduli of X with the sum of the moduli of the conformal pieces f, plus the gluing data along K.

First attempt. Count the number of moduli as Σ over non-disc f of (6g(f)+4ν(f)−6), plus a correction term that is struck out. This is a real dimension: Teichmüller space of a bordered surface of genus g(f) with ν(f) boundary circles, each boundary carrying one extra real marking parameter (6g−6+3ν, plus ν). The corrections come from the 'formes conformes' of the disc pieces.

Second attempt, for g ≥ 2, matching the complex dimension 3g−3 of M_g. Grothendieck uses the Euler characteristic relation 2−2g = Σ_f (2−2g(f)−ν(f)) + (1−λ), where λ is a numerical invariant of K. The page says 'nombre de composantes'; this only works if 1−λ = χ(K). He multiplies by 3/2 to get:

3g−3 = Σ_f [3(g(f)−1) + (3/2)ν(f)] + (3/2)(λ−1).

The summand 3g(f)−3+(3/2)ν(f) is half the real dimension 6g−6+3ν of the Teichmüller space of a bordered piece. A disc contributes −3/2, i.e. half of −3, the dimension of its real Möbius automorphism group. Separating the μ disc pieces gives

N = 3g−3 = Σ_{f non-disc}(3g(f)+(3/2)ν(f)−3) + (3/2)·(correction in λ, μ),

with some sign check '≥ 0'.

The genus-1 case is treated separately because of the extra automorphism (N−1). With g(f) = 0 always, the per-piece count is 4ν(f)−6, which he notes is ≥ 2, so non-disc pieces have ν ≥ 2.

So the page is a bookkeeping verification. Cutting a Riemann surface along K, the moduli of the conformal pieces (with boundary data) plus the gluing parameters recover the dimension of M_g. This is a dimension consistency check for a 'conformal surgery' description of moduli space.
errors: The Euler relation 2−2g = Σ(2−2g(f)−ν(f)) + 1−λ holds only if χ(K) = 1−λ, e.g. if K is connected with first Betti number λ. If λ is literally the number of connected components of K it fails. Counterexample: two parallel meridians on a torus give 0 ≠ −1. The reading of λ is ambiguous.

The first formula uses 6g(f)+4ν(f)−6 (real, with boundary markings). The second uses 3g(f)+(3/2)ν(f)−3, which is half of 6g−6+3ν, without markings. The two normalisations are inconsistent and the page does not reconcile them.

The final correction terms (3/2)(μ+λ) or similar, with a '?' and '≥0', and the g=1 formula 'N−1 = Σ(4ν−6) − 1' are tentative. The disc contribution should enter with a negative sign (−3/2 per disc), so the written '+ (3/2)(μ+λ)' looks doubtful.

ideas.what: Dimension count of M_g via cutting a Riemann surface along a subcomplex K into conformal pieces with boundary, using additivity of the Euler characteristic
ideas.modern_name: Additivity of Teichmüller dimensions under gluing / Fenchel–Nielsen-type parameter count for bordered surfaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Fricke–Klein, Fenchel–Nielsen; Bers; Abikoff for bordered surfaces)
ideas.where_published: Theme of conformal surgery hinted at in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but this computation is not there

ideas.what: Disc components counted with negative dimension −3 (real), i.e. −3/2 complex, from their Möbius automorphism group
ideas.modern_name: Virtual dimension of unstable pieces (automorphism correction)

ideas.what: Requiring the ends of complementary pieces to be homotopically non-trivial (no trivial discs) as a normalisation of the surgery data
ideas.modern_name: Essential multicurves/graphs; stability conditions on pieces

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine, partially erroneous parameter count checking that the moduli of the pieces of a cut Riemann surface add up to 3g−3. It is historically interesting as part of the conformal-surgery programme behind the Esquisse, but it contains nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Line 1–2 likely reads 'Vaut mieux dès lors exiger que ces bouts soient homotopiquement non triviaux…'.
The left margin note probably reads 'On rappelle X^0 := X formé des K… λ le nombre de composantes(?) de K', with λ's meaning uncertain.
In the g≥2 line the struck-out terms before 3/2(…) are partly legible; the last factor is something like (3/2)(μ+λ…), with a '?' and '≥ 0' added.
Under the g=1 formula, the brace under 4ν(f)−6 is annotated '≥ 2' (≥2 written as a small vertical ≥ and 2).
'pas un disque' under the sums is written 'f pas un disque' / 'f ≠ un disque'.
